turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one moment, this terminal has frozen again. Alright, Mr Krishnan, go ahead.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. The waiting hall was rather full, but never mind that. I have come regarding my diabetes, the sugar readings are not settling.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, type two diabetes. You are fifty-eight, is that right? What medicines are you on now?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I am fifty-eight. I am taking metformin tablets by mouth, one thousand milligrams in the morning and one thousand at night, and also insulin at bedtime. I have had diabetes for twelve years.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse has documented Lantus, insulin glargine, twenty-four units at bedtime. Kindly confirm that.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): With respect, Doctor, I must correct that. I am injecting eighteen units only, not twenty-four. Perhaps she has noted the previous dose.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eighteen? Sorry, repeat the number, I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Eighteen units of glargine at night, Doctor, on the nights I actually take it.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So I have twenty-four from the nurse and eighteen from you. Do you take that injection every night?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every night, I am afraid. On duty days I skip it. I leave very early, and I do not want a low sugar episode on the local train.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again. You skip it through the whole working week?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. Monday to Friday I usually omit it. On Saturday and Sunday I take the eighteen units properly.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): What has the home meter been showing? Fasting first, please.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Fasting was one-eighty-something. The display was faint, and I did not write it down. I am sorry.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Um, one-eighty? Sorry, can you give me the figure again. I only half heard, I was on the screen.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): It was one-eighty-something, well, actually around one hundred and eighty. Perhaps one eighty-four, or one eighty-six. I did not note it properly.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): And after food?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): After lunch it was two-hundred and something. I think near two twenty, but I am not fully sure, the reading had already gone off the screen.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with the feet? Tingling, wounds, pain when you walk?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I am having a mild tingling in the toes at night. There are no wounds, and there is no pain when I walk. There is no numbness as such.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has that tingling been there?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): It has been some months, Doctor. I cannot say precisely when it began.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the eyes? Any blurring, and when was the last retina check?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Vision is clear, no blurring. The last eye check was about two years ago. I am not certain of the exact month.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any low sugar recently? Shaking, sweating?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Once, last month, I felt shaky before lunch on a day I had taken the insulin. I took glucose and it passed. Nothing since then.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets? Blood pressure?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I also have high blood pressure, for about eight years. I take telmisartan forty milligrams by mouth each morning. They told me the pressure is controlled.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicine?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. I have no known allergies.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Looking at these sugars, I will raise the glargine to twenty-eight units every night, and I will see you back in two weeks.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, if you kindly increase it, I may go low on the days I do inject, and I am already missing the work-day doses. I thought I should mention that clearly.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ah, yes. I was still looking at the nurse's twenty-four. I think the high sugars are from the missed doses, not because your night dose is too small. We will not increase anything today, and we will not do that two-week visit I just said.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will continue the metformin as it is. Until the chart and your syringe agree, I am not changing the insulin, so keep drawing what you have been drawing. I do not want a jump to a higher dose on top of missed days.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): That is very fair, Doctor. I will follow whatever you advise.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am sending bloods today, HbA1c, a fasting glucose, and a creatinine. Please do not skip the injection on work days. Carry a small sweet if you are anxious on the train, and write the meter numbers in a notebook.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly. I will note them properly from tomorrow. I work in accounts, so a notebook is no trouble.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the tingling in the toes does not settle over the next few weeks, we might arrange a Doppler of the leg arteries, only to check the circulation. Not today.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. Only if it continues.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will refer you to ophthalmology for a retina check, since it has been about two years. Please attend that.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor, I will attend. Thank you for explaining it so patiently.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in four weeks with the reports. If anything feels like a low sugar before that, take glucose and let the clinic know.
